title: Non-text Content
review_questions: Does every meaningful image have a text alternative that conveys the same information?
Are decorative images hidden from assistive technology with empty alt or role=presentation?
Do icon buttons have an accessible name?
who_is_affected: Blind users and people who cannot see images rely on text alternatives to understand visual content.

title: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
review_questions: Is a text transcript or equivalent provided for prerecorded audio-only content?
Is a text alternative or audio track provided for prerecorded video-only content?
who_is_affected: Deaf or hard-of-hearing users and blind users cannot access audio or silent video without a text or audio alternative.

title: Captions (Prerecorded)
review_questions: Are captions provided for all prerecorded video that includes audio?
who_is_affected: Deaf and hard-of-hearing users cannot follow spoken content in video without captions.

title: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
review_questions: Is audio description or a full text alternative provided for prerecorded synchronized media?
who_is_affected: Blind users cannot perceive visual information in a video without an audio description or text alternative.

title: Captions (Live)
review_questions: Is live captioning provided for any live audio in synchronized media?
who_is_affected: Deaf and hard-of-hearing users cannot follow live audio streams without real-time captions.

title: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
review_questions: Is audio description provided for all prerecorded video in synchronized media?
who_is_affected: Blind users cannot access visual-only information in video without audio description.

title: Info and Relationships
review_questions: Are headings, lists, tables, and form fields marked up with the correct semantic HTML or ARIA roles?
Does visual structure (grouping, hierarchy, labels) have a programmatic equivalent?
Are form inputs associated with their visible labels?
who_is_affected: Screen reader users depend on semantic markup to understand the structure and relationships in a page.

title: Meaningful Sequence
review_questions: Does the DOM order match the visual reading order where sequence affects meaning?
Is CSS used to reorder content in a way that breaks logical reading order?
who_is_affected: Screen reader users and keyboard users encounter content in DOM order, so a mismatch with visual order causes confusion.

title: Sensory Characteristics
review_questions: Do any instructions refer solely to shape, color, size, or position without a text label?
For example, does the UI say 'click the green button' or 'use the icon on the right' without another identifier?
who_is_affected: Blind users and people with color blindness cannot rely on visual or spatial characteristics alone to identify controls.

title: Orientation
review_questions: Does the page or any component lock itself to portrait or landscape orientation without an essential reason?
who_is_affected: Users with limited mobility who have their device fixed in one orientation cannot use content that locks to the opposite orientation.

title: Identify Input Purpose
review_questions: Do input fields that collect personal data (name, email, address, phone) have the correct autocomplete attribute?
who_is_affected: People with cognitive disabilities and motor impairments benefit from browser autofill, which requires correct autocomplete values.

title: Use of Color
review_questions: Is color the only way to convey information, indicate an action, or distinguish an element?
Are error states, required fields, or status indicators differentiated by more than color alone (e.g., icon, label, pattern)?
who_is_affected: People with color blindness or low vision cannot distinguish meaning conveyed by color alone.

title: Audio Control
review_questions: Does any audio play automatically for more than 3 seconds?
If so, is there a mechanism to pause, stop, or control the volume independently of the system volume?
who_is_affected: Screen reader users are disrupted by auto-playing audio because it competes with their speech output.

title: Contrast (Minimum)
review_questions: Does normal text (below 18pt or 14pt bold) have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1?
Does large text have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1?
who_is_affected: People with low vision or color blindness struggle to read text that does not have sufficient contrast against its background.

title: Resize Text
review_questions: Does the page remain functional when text is zoomed to 200% using browser zoom?
Is any text clipped, overlapping, or cut off at 200% zoom?
who_is_affected: People with low vision increase text size in their browser, and content must remain usable when they do.

title: Images of Text
review_questions: Is text embedded in images where real HTML text could be used instead?
If an image of text is used, is it either customizable by the user or essential to the presentation?
who_is_affected: People with low vision who customise fonts or colors cannot do so with images of text.

title: Reflow
review_questions: Can all content be accessed without horizontal scrolling at a viewport width of 320 CSS pixels?
Does any component require two-dimensional scrolling at high zoom levels?
who_is_affected: People with low vision who zoom to 400% on a desktop effectively have a 320px viewport, and horizontal scrolling is a significant barrier.

title: Non-text Contrast
review_questions: Do UI component boundaries (button borders, input outlines, checkbox edges) have at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors?
Do graphical elements required to understand content (chart lines, icons) have at least 3:1 contrast?
who_is_affected: People with low vision may not perceive control boundaries or icons that lack sufficient contrast.

title: Text Spacing
review_questions: When line-height is set to 1.5x font size, letter-spacing to 0.12x, word-spacing to 0.16x, and paragraph spacing to 2x font size, does the content remain readable with no clipping or overlap?
who_is_affected: People with dyslexia and low vision often override text spacing, and content must not break when they do.

title: Content on Hover or Focus
review_questions: Can the user dismiss hover/focus-triggered content (like a tooltip) without moving focus?
Can the pointer move over hover-triggered content without it disappearing?
Does the tooltip or popup remain visible until the user dismisses it or moves focus away?
who_is_affected: Users with low vision who zoom in and users with motor disabilities often need to move the pointer to read tooltip content.

title: Keyboard
review_questions: Can every interactive element (links, buttons, form fields, custom widgets) be reached and activated by keyboard alone?
Is any functionality triggered only by mouse hover or pointer events with no keyboard equivalent?
who_is_affected: Keyboard-only users, switch access users, and screen reader users cannot use a mouse and depend entirely on keyboard access.

title: No Keyboard Trap
review_questions: Can keyboard focus move out of every component using standard keys (Tab, Shift+Tab, Escape)?
Are there any modals, date pickers, or custom widgets that trap focus permanently?
who_is_affected: Keyboard users become stuck on the page if they cannot move focus out of a component.

title: Character Key Shortcuts
review_questions: Does the UI implement single-character keyboard shortcuts (letters, numbers, punctuation)?
If so, can the user turn them off or remap them to require a modifier key?
who_is_affected: Speech input users may accidentally trigger single-key shortcuts while dictating, and keyboard users may trigger them unintentionally.

title: Timing Adjustable
review_questions: Does the page or any component impose a time limit on the user?
If yes, can the user turn it off, adjust it to at least 10x the default, or extend it with a simple action?
who_is_affected: People with cognitive or motor disabilities need more time to complete tasks and may be unable to act before a session or form expires.

title: Pause, Stop, Hide
review_questions: Does the page include any moving, blinking, or scrolling content that starts automatically and lasts more than 5 seconds?
Is there a mechanism to pause, stop, or hide it?
who_is_affected: People with attention or seizure disorders and screen reader users are disrupted by auto-moving content they cannot stop.

title: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
review_questions: Does any content flash more than three times per second?
who_is_affected: People with photosensitive epilepsy can experience seizures triggered by rapidly flashing content.

title: Bypass Blocks
review_questions: Is there a skip-navigation link or landmark structure that lets keyboard users bypass repeated navigation blocks?
who_is_affected: Keyboard and screen reader users must tab through every navigation item on every page load unless a bypass mechanism exists.

title: Page Titled
review_questions: Does the page have a title element that describes its topic or purpose?
who_is_affected: Screen reader users and keyboard users rely on the page title to identify the page, especially when switching between tabs.

title: Focus Order
review_questions: When navigating by Tab, does focus move in a logical order that matches the visual layout?
After opening a dialog or modal, does focus move into it and return to the trigger on close?
who_is_affected: Keyboard users and screen reader users become confused when focus jumps unpredictably around the page.

title: Link Purpose (In Context)
review_questions: Can the purpose of each link be understood from its text alone or from its surrounding context?
Are there multiple 'Read more' or 'Click here' links that do not describe where they lead?
who_is_affected: Screen reader users often navigate by listing all links on a page; ambiguous link text makes it impossible to choose the right one.

title: Multiple Ways
review_questions: Is more than one way available to reach a page within the site (e.g., navigation menu, search, sitemap)?
who_is_affected: People with cognitive disabilities and motor impairments benefit from alternative ways to find content when one navigation method is difficult.

title: Headings and Labels
review_questions: Do headings accurately describe the content that follows them?
Do form field labels clearly describe the purpose of each input?
who_is_affected: Screen reader users navigate by headings and labels; vague or missing text makes it hard to find and understand content.

title: Focus Visible
review_questions: Is the keyboard focus indicator visible on all interactive elements?
Has outline: none or outline: 0 been applied without a replacement focus style?
who_is_affected: Keyboard users cannot tell which element is active without a visible focus indicator.

title: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
review_questions: When an element receives keyboard focus, is any part of it still visible (not entirely hidden by sticky headers, cookie banners, or modals)?
Do fixed or sticky elements overlap focused components in a way that hides them completely?
who_is_affected: Keyboard users cannot interact with a focused element they cannot see on screen.

title: Pointer Gestures
review_questions: Does any feature require a multipoint gesture (pinch, two-finger scroll) or a path-based gesture (swipe, draw)?
If yes, is there a single-pointer alternative for the same action?
who_is_affected: People with motor disabilities may be unable to perform complex gestures and need simpler single-tap or single-click alternatives.

title: Pointer Cancellation
review_questions: Are actions triggered on the down-event (mousedown/touchstart) without the ability to cancel?
For single-pointer actions, does the up-event complete the function or allow undo?
who_is_affected: People with motor disabilities may accidentally touch or click controls and need to be able to abort the action before releasing.

title: Label in Name
review_questions: For buttons or links with a visible text label, does the accessible name (aria-label, aria-labelledby) contain that visible text?
Is there an icon button whose aria-label is completely different from any visible text near it?
who_is_affected: Speech input users activate controls by speaking their visible label; if the accessible name differs, the voice command fails.

title: Motion Actuation
review_questions: Does any feature respond to device motion (shake, tilt) or user motion?
If yes, is there a UI alternative and can the motion response be disabled?
who_is_affected: People who use their device on a mount or have tremors cannot perform or prevent unintended motion-triggered actions.

title: Dragging Movements
review_questions: Does any feature require dragging (drag-and-drop, sliders moved by dragging) as the only means of operation?
Is there a single-pointer alternative (e.g., up/down buttons, input field) for every dragging function?
who_is_affected: People with motor disabilities often cannot perform dragging movements and need non-drag alternatives.

title: Target Size (Minimum)
review_questions: Are interactive targets at least 24x24 CSS pixels in size?
If a target is smaller, is it spaced far enough from other targets so that a 24px-diameter circle around it does not overlap another target?
who_is_affected: People with limited motor control struggle to accurately tap or click small targets, especially on touch screens.

title: Language of Page
review_questions: Does the html element have a valid lang attribute that identifies the primary language of the page?
who_is_affected: Screen readers use the language attribute to select the correct voice and pronunciation rules; without it, content may be spoken incorrectly.

title: Language of Parts
review_questions: Are passages in a different language from the page's default marked with a lang attribute on the containing element?
who_is_affected: Screen reader users hear garbled pronunciation when foreign-language passages lack a lang attribute.

title: On Focus
review_questions: Does focusing on any component (e.g., a select, link, or input) automatically trigger a page navigation or major context change without user action?
who_is_affected: Keyboard users and screen reader users are disoriented when focus alone causes an unexpected page change.

title: On Input
review_questions: Does changing the value of a form component (e.g., selecting from a dropdown) automatically submit a form or navigate the page without the user being warned in advance?
who_is_affected: Keyboard users and people with cognitive disabilities are disoriented by unexpected navigation triggered by input changes.

title: Consistent Navigation
review_questions: Does the navigation appear in the same relative order across all pages of the site?
who_is_affected: People with cognitive disabilities and screen reader users build a mental map of a site based on consistent navigation placement.

title: Consistent Identification
review_questions: Are components with the same function labeled and identified the same way across the site (e.g., a search field always labeled 'Search')?
who_is_affected: People with cognitive disabilities rely on consistent naming to learn and remember how to use recurring components.

title: Consistent Help
review_questions: If the site provides help mechanisms (chat, contact link, FAQ), do they appear in the same position on every page where they are present?
who_is_affected: People with cognitive disabilities can find help more reliably when its location is predictable across pages.

title: Error Identification
review_questions: When a form error is detected automatically, is the field in error identified and the error described in text?
Is the error message conveyed by more than color alone?
who_is_affected: Blind users and people with cognitive disabilities need errors described in text to understand what went wrong and which field to correct.

title: Labels or Instructions
review_questions: Does every form input have a visible label or clear instructions describing what the user should enter?
Are placeholder texts used as the only label? (Placeholder disappears on input, which is insufficient.)
who_is_affected: People with cognitive disabilities and screen reader users need labels to understand what each form field expects.

title: Error Suggestion
review_questions: When a form validation error is known (e.g., invalid email format), is a specific correction suggestion provided to the user?
who_is_affected: People with cognitive disabilities and screen reader users need concrete suggestions to correct mistakes without having to guess.

title: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
review_questions: For forms that complete purchases, make legal commitments, or delete user data, is the user given a chance to review, confirm, or reverse the submission?
who_is_affected: People with cognitive disabilities and motor disabilities are more likely to make accidental submissions and need a way to correct or undo them.

title: Redundant Entry
review_questions: In a multi-step process, is the user ever asked to enter information they already provided in an earlier step?
If so, is the earlier value auto-populated or available to select?
who_is_affected: People with cognitive disabilities and motor impairments are burdened by re-typing information the system already has.

title: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
review_questions: Does the authentication flow require the user to memorize a password or solve a cognitive puzzle without offering an alternative (such as a password manager or copy-paste)?
Is copy-paste disabled on password or authentication fields?
who_is_affected: People with cognitive disabilities, dyslexia, or memory impairments struggle to remember passwords and need alternative authentication methods.

title: Name, Role, Value
review_questions: Do all interactive components have an accessible name, a correct role, and programmatically exposed state?
Are custom components (built with div or span) given the correct ARIA role, states, and properties?
who_is_affected: Screen reader users rely on name, role, and value to understand and interact with every control on the page.

title: Status Messages
review_questions: When status messages appear without focus moving to them (e.g., 'Item added to cart', form success banners, loading spinners), do they use role=status, role=alert, or aria-live so screen readers announce them?
who_is_affected: Blind users do not see status messages that appear on screen; without a live region, they have no way of knowing an action succeeded or failed.
